html:
British East Africa, officially the East Africa Protectorate, was the British territory from the Indian Ocean to Lake Victoria, from 1895 to 1920, when it became the colony of Kenya. The map shows it in 1914.

It grew out of the Imperial British East Africa Company, which went bankrupt, and the government took over in 1895. The coastal strip around Mombasa was leased from the Sultan of Zanzibar.

To reach Uganda, Britain built the Uganda Railway from Mombasa to Lake Victoria between 1896 and 1901, using thousands of workers brought from India. Nairobi, a railway camp, became the capital in 1905. The government then gave the cool highlands to white settlers, pushing the Kikuyu, Maasai and others off their land. The Nandi fought the railway for years until their leader Koitalel Arap Samoei was killed in 1905. Land became the great grievance that later fed the Mau Mau rising.
sum: British East Africa, officially the East Africa Protectorate, was the British territory from the Indian Ocean to Lake Victoria, from 1895 to 1920, when it became the colony of Kenya. The map shows it in 1914.
